Subject: Interlock: closure catalogue + exec asks for QBR prep

Team —

Thanks for the sync this morning. I pulled together the items we agreed to close before the QBR (start of next month) and flagged the few exec-level asks that need sponsor confirmation. Goal: get owners committed and a minimal mitigation path for anything we won't close by the QBR.

Quick summary of owners + asks (attached tracker + register):
- Marissa: finalize launch criteria for Dedicated burst policy (due 5/25) — action: one-pager for SLAs + rollback guardrails.
- Karthik: validate regression signal for latency after planned quantization (due 5/24) — action: short eval plan + threshold.
- Vivek: confirm on-call escalation path for inter-region fallback (due 5/28) — action: runbook draft.

External items to call out: AtlasHealth procurement still has an open question on data residency for Dedicated nodes (Emily copied). Procurement (ProcureCo) is asking for the SOC2 artifact handoff timeline.

Please reply inline with any changes to due dates or owners. I attached: QBR_Roadmap_Deck_v3.pdf (slides), Exec_Asks_Register.xlsx (spreadsheet), and the interlock-closure-tracker.csv (current state).

Thanks —

Vanessa / Marissa —

Quick update on the quantization regression check: I ran the smoke eval on the min-prod prompt set and saw a 3.8% latency uplift in p95 for the 8-bit profile on the small LLM variant. That exceeds our near-term threshold of 3%.

Proposed next steps:
1) Temporarily pin AtlasHealth workload to the float16 variant for the canary (timeline: 48 hours)
2) Run the extended regression suite across full prompt set (48–72 hours)
3) If regression persists, open an inf-ops rollback ticket and schedule a targeted kernel patch.

I documented the eval steps and raw numbers in a short doc and added the row to Exec_Asks_Register.xlsx under "quantization-regression". If execs want a simpler mitigation, we can propose a short-term dedicated float16 window for high-value accounts.

-kar
Karthik Iyer

Redwood Inference
